text:
sam: heads up — running into a weird logging/redaction mismatch in the sample apps. server logs sometimes show x-request-id as REDACTED but our trace viewer has the real id. repro is on node + python SDKs behind the same gateway.

maria: hmm, is the redaction happening in the SDK or at the logging hook? any snippets?

sam: minimal repro: request hits gateway -> we set header x-request-id=abc123 -> node service logs req.headers and shows REDACTED, but otel span.attributes has abc123. looks like hooks run in different order. snippet:```js
// express middleware
app.use((req,res,next)=>{ req.headers['x-request-id']='abc123'; next(); });
app.use(instrumentation.middleware()); // otel auto-instrumentation
app.use(logHook); // our log hook scrubs headers
```

alex: aha — we've seen ordering races before. Node SDK's autoinstrumentation attaches spans during http instrumentation which can capture headers before our scrub hook runs. so logs can show scrubbed value while trace retains original if span created earlier.

dinesh: the odd part is python behaves differently: python's OTEL hook seems to read headers after our scrub and then sets span attr to REDACTED. so parity is off between runtimes.

sam: yes — parity problem. customer-facing telemetry shows different request ids depending on stack. bad for correlating traces -> logs.

maria: quick mitigation: make our scrub idempotent and store the canonical id on req.ctx or res.locals before scrubbing headers, then have both log hook and otel hook read from that canonical place. less brittle than relying on middleware order.

alex: agreed. also file a follow-up to make SDKs expose a small API: setCanonicalRequestId(req, id) — this avoids header mutation surprises.

ci-bot: created issue #4127: devex: canonical-request-id-api + investigation into otel hook ordering (link: https://go/repo/4127) :white_check_mark:

dinesh: I can prototype a tiny shim in node AND python sample apps this afternoon. will also add a test that asserts logs+spans share the same id.

sam: thanks — for the immediate deploy, can we add a quick kludge: if header x-request-id missing in logs, fall back to span attribute 'http.request_id' to display in dashboards? saves customers while we patch SDKs.

maria: yes, I'll add a transient fallback in the logging pipeline and add a note in sampleapp README about the hook-ordering gotcha.

alex: FYI this intersects with redaction policy: ensure we never write raw IDs to long-term logs. canonical id should be hashed when persisted. add that to the issue.

sam: good call. leaving PR comments on #4127 after the prototype. thanks all :raised_hands:
